title: Love God, Serve Man -- Ch. 13: A Salute to ASTA
keywords: equality, of freedom and of fairness
primary_topics: Chapter 13 of 'Love God, Serve Man' -- CJP's acceptance speech of November 15, 1985 at the closing session of the 55th ASTA World Travel Congress in Rome, on being elected chairman of the International Council of Governors of the American Society of Travel Agents, the first and only Filipino to hold that post.

His reading of the election as 'a triumph of the American dream' of equality, freedom and fairness -- invoking Jefferson's 'all men are equal,' Lincoln's word to the lowliest, and Lee Iacocca's 'American religion of fairness' from that week's keynote.

His stated mission as chairman: to secure for ASTA's international members the same benefits their American counterparts enjoy, modified to their own needs and objectives, beginning with the seminars of the 14th International Conference in Athens.
sub_topics: He thanks the international members and his colleagues on the International Council of Governors, calls himself inadequate and overwhelmed by the responsibility, and takes the honor as 'a tribute to my country and to my people.'
He frames his election as a vindication of the American dream in which 'even the lowliest in society' may aspire to lead, serve and succeed.

He grounds that dream in three American voices: Jefferson writing that '(A)ll men are equal,' Lincoln telling the lowliest 'Chin up, for you are free forever,' and Lee Iacocca preaching 'the American religion of fairness' in his keynote address that Monday.
He credits ASTA as a most successful national association whose members enjoy its full benefits, whether political action in the US Congress or educational seminars at the World Travel Congress.

He defines his duty as ensuring international members receive the same benefits, 'but modified to meet their specific objectives,' and announces that the seminars of the 14th International Conference in Athens next February 22-26 will be tailored accordingly.

He closes with a pledge of international cooperation and support, arguing that combining the American dream of equality, freedom and fairness with that pledge will produce 'the greatest international society of travel professionals in the world,' and salutes the congress from the Philippines and from Baron Travel Corporation: 'Mabuhay ASTA!'

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 13 of 'Love God, Serve Man' is the short acceptance speech CJP delivered on November 15, 1985 at the closing session of the 55th ASTA World Travel Congress in Rome, after his election as chairman of the International Council of Governors of the American Society of Travel Agents. He thanked the international members and his fellow governors for giving him 'the highest position within their authority,' confessed that he felt inadequate and overwhelmed by the responsibility, and insisted that the honor was 'not only for me personally but is, in fact, a tribute to my country and to my people.' He read his election as 'a triumph of the American dream' in which even the lowliest may aspire to lead, serve and succeed -- the dream he attributed to Thomas Jefferson writing that all men are equal, to Abraham Lincoln telling the lowliest 'Chin up, for you are free forever,' and to Lee Iacocca, who had invoked 'the American religion of fairness' in his keynote earlier that week. Granting that ASTA had served its American members well, whether through political action in the US Congress or educational seminars at the World Travel Congress, he defined his own mission as pleading that same religion of fairness so that international members would receive equal benefits, modified to their specific objectives -- beginning with seminars retooled for the 14th International Conference in Athens that February, to which he invited all delegates. He closed by pledging the international members' cooperation and support under his incumbency, arguing that this mixture of the American dream of equality, freedom and fairness with international solidarity would build the greatest international society of travel professionals in the world, and saluted the congress from the Philippines and from Baron Travel Corporation: 'Mabuhay ASTA!'
